method.method_draft: Read the image as an ogive/cumulative relative frequency plot with Score on the horizontal axis and Percentile on the vertical axis. Observe that the curve rises most steeply for relatively low-to-middle scores, roughly from the teens through the 30s, and then becomes nearly flat over a long stretch of higher scores, extending toward about 90. Use the rule that the slope of a cumulative relative frequency curve represents where the original data are concentrated: steep parts mean many observations, flat parts mean few observations spread out. Since most scores are clustered at lower/middle values and a small number of scores extend far to the high-score side, conclude that the distribution has a long right tail, so it is skewed to the right.
